# githubsettings_organization_recorded_settings (Resource)

Records the organization settings listed in the schema below without changing them. Set each argument to the value GitHub reports. Apply fails while the configured values differ. Use a token with organization Administration read access.

Removing this resource from Terraform management leaves the GitHub setting in place.

## Import the current setting

Read the current values with the GitHub CLI. Set [`GITHUB_TOKEN`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elephant-evergreen/githubsettings/latest/docs#authentication) first so this command and Terraform use the same token. Replace `OWNER`.

```shell
GH_TOKEN="${GITHUB_TOKEN:?Set GITHUB_TOKEN first}" gh api --hostname github.com orgs/OWNER \
  -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10" \
  --jq '{
  default_repository_branch,
  members_can_change_repo_visibility,
  members_can_create_teams,
  members_can_delete_issues,
  members_can_delete_repositories,
  members_can_invite_outside_collaborators,
  members_can_view_dependency_insights,
  readers_can_create_discussions,
  secret_scanning_validity_checks_enabled,
  two_factor_requirement_enabled
}'
```

Use the returned values as resource arguments. If an expected field is `null`, check the token's organization Administration access and the [response for your organization](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/orgs#get-an-organization).

Add the import block below to a Terraform project configured with `elephant-evergreen/githubsettings`. The [quickstart](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elephant-evergreen/githubsettings/latest/docs#import-a-policy) shows the provider block and initialization. Replace the example ID and address with those of your resource.

```terraform
import {
  to = githubsettings_organization_recorded_settings.example
  id = "example-owner"
}
```

1. Add the resource block with arguments that match the current GitHub values.
2. Run `terraform plan -out=adopt.tfplan` and keep a plan that contains only the import. If it proposes a change, compare the differing values with the current policy and save a new plan.
3. Apply the saved plan.

## Example configuration

```terraform
resource "githubsettings_organization_recorded_settings" "example" {
  owner                                    = "example-owner"
  default_repository_branch                = "main"
  members_can_change_repo_visibility       = false
  members_can_create_teams                 = false
  members_can_delete_issues                = false
  members_can_delete_repositories          = false
  members_can_invite_outside_collaborators = false
  members_can_view_dependency_insights     = false
  readers_can_create_discussions           = false
  secret_scanning_validity_checks_enabled  = false
  two_factor_requirement_enabled           = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `default_repository_branch` (String) Default branch name for new repositories.
- `members_can_change_repo_visibility` (Boolean) Allow members to change repository visibility.
- `members_can_create_teams` (Boolean) Allow members to create teams.
- `members_can_delete_issues` (Boolean) Allow members to delete issues.
- `members_can_delete_repositories` (Boolean) Allow members to delete repositories.
- `members_can_invite_outside_collaborators` (Boolean) Allow members to invite outside collaborators.
- `members_can_view_dependency_insights` (Boolean) Allow members to view dependency insights.
- `owner` (String) GitHub account that owns the repository or organization.
- `readers_can_create_discussions` (Boolean) Allow users with read access to create discussions.
- `secret_scanning_validity_checks_enabled` (Boolean) Whether secret scanning validity checks are enabled.
- `two_factor_requirement_enabled` (Boolean) Whether two-factor authentication is required.
